Lolland is a Danish municipality featured in the 2022–2023 Annual Report from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) [^src1]. The report serves as a critical tool for local quality development and benchmarking within the Danish healthcare system, evaluating the clinical quality of atrial fibrillation treatment across national, regional, and all 98 municipal levels using data from the Danish National Patient Register (LPR) and the Danish Stroke Registry (DanStroke) [^src1].

In the context of the report, Lolland's data regarding stroke (apoplexy) events among atrial fibrillation patients is specifically utilized in the calculations for Indicator 5, which tracks the prevention of ischemic strokes via anticoagulant (AC) treatment [^src1]. On page 94, Lolland's municipal performance is detailed in a data table where it is marked as not meeting the indicator's target ("Nej") [^src1]. The registry recorded 16 stroke events among a cohort of 1,425 patients (yielding a rate of 1.1) for one measure, and 11 events among 1,439 patients (a rate of 0.8) for another [^src1].
